title: The Wisp That Learned to Split
story: In the Glass Orchard, Mr 6 meets Pallowreave the Thorn Wisp, a prickly ball of blue light that splits into 3 whenever a blade touches it. A frightened orchard-keeper warns that the wisps only vanish for good if the swarm can be counted before the last split — so Mr 6 sheathes his sword and starts thinking.
question: There is 1 wisp now. If Mr 6 strikes, every wisp present splits into 3, and he plans to strike 4 times in a row. Each wisp in the final swarm must be trapped in a jar that holds 9 wisps. How many jars are needed?
solution: Each strike triples the swarm: 1 * 3 * 3 * 3 * 3 = 81 wisps after four strikes.
Each jar holds 9 wisps: 81 / 9 = 9 jars exactly.
praise: Tripling four times was the hard part and you tracked the growth well — the last step was packing those wisps into jars of 9.
hint: Multiply by 3 once for each strike, then see how many groups of 9 that total makes.
victory: Mr 6 lined up nine jars, tapped the wisp exactly four times, and clapped the lids shut as the last spark drifted in. Pallowreave now glows politely as an orchard night-light.
imagePrompt: A small numeral-six knight in a moonlit orchard of glass-leaved trees, calmly holding out rows of glowing jars as a prickly blue wisp bursts into a shimmering cloud of triplets.
